title: Pre-Analysis — Interfay Sealing and Corrosion Protection of the Fwd Lower Shell Lap Joints
abstract: Original pre-analysis of the interfay sealing and protection change on the forward lower shell lap joints, covering the inspection and blend-out content it displaces and the published skin repair it has to coexist with.

sections.objective: Establish what has to change around a proposal to renew the interfay sealant and the protection scheme on the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joints, on the aircraft where filiform corrosion has been reported repeatedly at the same fastener rows. The design content is straightforward; the pre-analysis question is what the change does to the inspection interval that operators are currently flying, and whether an aircraft that has already been repaired locally can take it at all.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed. The high frequency eddy current inspection of the lap joint fasteners is the task the change is meant to relieve, and its interval is written into operator programmes; changing the joint without changing the interval leaves the fleet doing an inspection for a condition that has been removed. The part list figure for the skin panels and the joint carries the current splice plate and sealant items and would need a post-change configuration. The blend-out task for corrosion adjacent to the joint uses the same skin item and has to be sequenced against the resealing rather than performed after it. The published flush bonded repair on the same panel does not share a single identifier with the change and was found only by its description, but an aircraft carrying it has a bond line in the area the sealant renewal disturbs.
sections.next_steps: Ask continued airworthiness to state the post-change inspection interval before the modification is released, so that the two arrive together. Raise a part list change request for the post-change configuration. Add a note to the blend-out task requiring it to be completed before resealing rather than after. Obtain a repair design position on aircraft carrying the flush bonded patch, and reflect the answer in the retrofit bulletin as an assessment step.

similarity_seeds: filiform corrosion at a forward fuselage longitudinal joint
eddy current inspection interval on lap joint fastener rows
bonded repair patch on a thinned lower shell skin

tasks.title: Establish the current inspection programme on the affected joint
Review part list and blend-out content on the same panel
Search published repairs on the forward lower shell

expected_findings.rationale: The eddy current inspection of the joint fastener rows is the task the change is intended to relieve, and its interval sits in operator maintenance programmes. Releasing the change without a revised interval leaves the fleet inspecting for a condition that has been designed out.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a post-change interval from continued airworthiness and release it with the modification.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries the current splice plate and sealant items as a single configuration. The change alters both and the figure has no way to show a pre and post state on this sheet.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a part list change request for a post-change configuration sheet.

expected_findings.rationale: The blend-out task for corrosion adjacent to the joint works the same skin item. Performed after resealing it destroys the new sealant line; performed before, it is free.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a sequencing note requiring blend-out to precede resealing.

evidence.similarity_note: Found only by the descriptive text. The repair speaks of a flush bonded patch for a thinned or cracked lower forward barrel skin; the change speaks of interfay sealant renewal and splice plate protection at the longitudinal joint. No part number, drawing, functional item number or zone is shared.

expected_findings.rationale: An aircraft carrying the flush patch has a bond line in the material the sealant renewal disturbs, and the effect of the sealant primer on that bond line has never been assessed.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a repair design position and add a repair assessment step to the retrofit bulletin.

expected_non_findings.reason: Reads almost identically to the forward shell repair — an external doubler at a longitudinal seam — and shares the standard practices secondary chapter, but it applies to the aft fuselage skin panels. There is no shared zone, part number or drawing with section 13.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position subject to the revised inspection interval being released with the modification and to a repair assessment step covering patched panels.
